paragraphs.text: Universes Within is the collective name for rebranded Magic multiverse versions of Universes Beyond cards. The term was first coined by Scryfall , and then occasionally adopted by Wizards of the Coast internally. It is not an official product name. When Wizards of the Coast started bringing rebranded sets to LGSs, the "SLX program" name was used. Cards printed under this program all had the set code "SLX".

The non-canon cards and the rebranded cards are considered equivalent game pieces, meaning you can only play up to four copies total of the rebranded version and Universes Beyond version combined in your deck. The Information below the text box has the special SLX set code and the SLD card number that it equals. All rebranded cards have the same rarity as the original. If a Universes Beyond card with an IP-specific creature type (e.g. astartes ) would be rebranded, it would receive a brand new creature type in the rebranded version. The <IP name> and <unique new creature type> would be one-for-one in the rules much like the names of the Godzilla skinned cards .

In 2021, Wizards of the Coast pledged to create and print in-multiverse versions of mechanically unique non-canon Secret Lair cards, approximately six months after their original release of the Secret Lair. These would become available as part of The List , and were said to be findable in Set Boosters for as long as players still were interested in opening them.

At their introduction, one in eight Set Boosters contained one of these cards, while another one in eight set boosters would contain a different card from the List. According to Mark Heggen , R&D wanted the in-world equivalents those to be around and people able to get their hands on them. They were not meant to be the ‘chase objects’. After 10 years, they wanted the "other-IP" ones "to be the cool ones that had a little bit more cachet and would be a bit more interesting to see". The in-world equivalents would be the ones that were there for people who were just looking for the gameplay.

In November 2024, Wizards of the Coast went back on the promise to always create Universes Within versions of mechanically unique Secret Lair cards. Mark Rosewater explained that since The List and Set Boosters had been phased out, Wizards was in a conundrum. Although they still wanted to create non-Secret Lair versions, they could no longer guarantee that these would always be different from what the Secret Lair had offered. They might keep the same name, and represent the same character/object/place - hence, it wouldn't always be a “Universe Within” version. This came true with the release of the Spring Flourishes promo cards in January 2025, which were still part of the D&D universe. In addition, it was announced that upcoming mechanically unique Secret Lair cards would become available for purchase in local WPN stores . The selected Secret Lair Drops available for WPN stores to sell will be identical to the non-foil Drops available on the Secret Lair website. This implied that no more future Secret Lairs would be rebranded. However, Mark Rosewater later stated that they are still able and, on occasion, will reprint cards in a Universes Within version.

In April 2025, Wizards of the Coast announced Through the Omenpaths , a series of digital sets that were Universes Within versions of Universes Beyond sets that otherwise wouldn't be coming to digital Magic platforms. These digital cards were mechanically identical to their Universes Beyond tabletop counterparts but with unique creative treatments, different art, and different names. This experiment was ultimately short-lived, as Wizards of the Coast secured digital rights for Marvel sets prior to the release of Marvel Super Heroes .
In June 2026, Mark Rosewater stated the goal for in-Multiverse sets to be more adventurous mechanically (on average) than Universes Beyond.

Wizards of the Coast originally did only commit to do Universes Within versions of Secret Lairs. Larger Universes Beyond sets like Warhammer 40K , Lord of the Rings and Doctor Who wouldn't receive 1:1 Universe Within versions, but R&D reserved the right to make them for individual cards if the need arose. According to Mark Rosewater , the biggest problem, from a business standpoint, with making a Universes Within card for every Universes Beyond card was that there wasn’t a large enough audience to offset the huge cost of such an undertaking. So far, only cards with non-IP specific names have been reprinted. This avoided the need to rename them.

Through the Omenpaths sets, introduced in 2025, were planned to be Universes Within versions of Universes Beyond sets that otherwise wouldn't be coming to digital Magic platforms. These digital cards were mechanically identical to their Universes Beyond tabletop counterparts but with unique creative treatments, different art, and different names. Through the Omenpaths sets were not planned for every Universes Beyond set, but rather only the ones that would not be coming to digital platforms (for example, because of digital licensing issues).

The first and only set to receive a Through the Omenpaths release was Marvel's Spider-Man . Though the exact behind-the-scenes details are unknown, Wizards of the Coast announced roughly one month prior to the release of Marvel Super Heroes that both that set and all future Marvel sets would be released on MTG Arena and Magic Online , thus eliminating any need for Through the Omenpaths sets moving forward. Additionally, Marvel's Spider-Man was released retroactively on both of these digital clients, though the Through the Omenpaths versions remain available in some form on both clients for players who prefer those versions.

Since Marvel properties were the only properties that were ever (publicly) planned to have Through the Omenpaths versions, there are currently no known upcoming Through the Omenpaths sets. Individual Through the Omenpaths cards may be reprinted in paper.

When Wizards of the Coast reprinted the Universes Within card Arvinox, the Mind Flail as part of the Miracle Worker Duskmourn: House of Horror Commander deck, the information below the text box that the card equals to SLD #340 ( Mind Flayer, the Shadow ) was left off in error. Wizards of the Coast planned to address future situations using a game rule update.

Because it's not rebranded as a different character, Themberchaud is officially the only card in the SLX program without an interchangeable name or the set code equivalence information below the text box .

In December 2025, a card named "Nishka, Pinnacle Cosmonaut" was noticed in Magic Online . It had the SLX code "=SLD 1501", making it the Universes Within version of Lara Croft, Tomb Raider . This card stopped being visible shortly afterwards, but has been confirmed to still be in the files by data miners. The card can also still be named by effects such as Pithing Needle that ask you to name a card.
